title: Microsoft's Maia 300 rack: 96 accelerators, HBM4, mostly liquid-cooled
summary: Microsoft has released architecture details for Maia 300, its third-generation Azure AI accelerator. The design pairs 96 accelerators per rack with a two-tier network that links up to 12,288 accelerators into a single superpod. The company says the system is built for cloud-scale agentic inference, and that it co-designed the software, silicon, rack infrastructure, networking, and data centers to run as one platform.

title: China proposes physical controls and tougher testing for new vehicles
summary: China proposed tighter vehicle design and safety requirements that would restrict fully hidden door handles, virtual controls for critical functions and several interior features in new vehicles. title: EU caps annual HEV imports at 350,000 to curb trade deficit with China
summary: The European Union plans to cap imports of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) at 350,000 units per year, with safeguard measures potentially taking effect as early as December 1, 2026. The four-year framework sets a 350,000-unit limit in its first year, followed by a 6% annual quota expansion starting in the second year, while both sides commit to complying with World Trade Organization (WTO) rules.

title: How 'Filter Moore's Law' is doubling revenue for a Taiwan chip filter maker
summary: Under what the industry terms the "Filter Moore's Law," each process node shrink lowers tolerance for airborne molecular contaminants, causing filtration demand to grow exponentially. summary: Largan chairman and CEO Adam Lin said October 2026 orders are tracking at roughly the same level as September's, but will begin declining in November as customers cut their forecasts after new phones went on sale. The comments signal that demand across the smartphone supply chain will weaken in the fourth quarter of 2026, creating challenges for handset chipmakers and other suppliers that performed strongly during the third quarter.

title: Microsoft calls for observable AI systems with emergency shutdown controls
summary: Microsoft urged organizations to design artificial intelligence systems as observable, controllable infrastructure rather than opaque "black boxes," arguing that people must be able to monitor model behavior and stop it during an emergency. The company said the approach should apply to enterprise AI systems as they are tested, deployed, and connected to business data and tools.
